T100000130583.name: Iran NIOC LNG Terminal
hw: 5 gas turbine units + 2 steam turbine units (CCGT, aggregate 1,130 MW: 5x162 MW + 2x160 MW nameplate), built as the Iran LNG project's own power-station package (project Package I-C, 'E-LNG': Power Station, Electric Motors and Compressors) starting 2007; EPC by MAPNA-group subsidiary Nirpars/Neyr Perse. Also carries 4 dedicated 3.3 MVA diesel gensets for site emergency backup (diesel-only, does not itself satisfy the fuel gate, but confirms an ongoing captive electrical relationship to the LNG site).
notes: This is the Iran LNG project at Tombak (owner match: IGEC 49% / Oil Industry Investment Co ~50% / Oil Industry Pension Fund 1%, matching GEM's listed owners almost exactly). The project's own design package included a dedicated on-site 1,130 MW CCGT power station (5 gas + 2 steam turbines) purpose-built to power the LNG plant, engineered/constructed by MAPNA-group companies from 2007. Because the LNG trains themselves have never started up (project suspended by the client since mid-2013 under sanctions), the completed power-plant units have instead been connected to Iran's national grid unit-by-unit since ~2022 to help meet national demand — but the plant was designed, sited, and built as this project's captive power block, which is a documented YES on design per SOP (as-designed captive power counts; partial/full grid export does not defeat a purpose-built captive finding).

T100000130916.name: South Pars LNG Terminal
hw: 1,000 MW combined-cycle gas turbine power plant, described as built 'to provide power for the project' (project design table, OGJ 2010). Turbine count/model not disclosed in the source found.
notes: This is the 'Pars LNG' project (owner match confirms: NIOC 50%, Total 30%, Petronas 20% — matching GEM's listed owners), a two-train (10 MMTPA) LNG project at Tombak fed by South Pars Phase 11. Oil & Gas Journal's 2010 project-by-project design summary states: 'It is noteworthy that a 1,000-Mw power plant utilizing combined-cycle gas turbines will provide power for the project' — an on-site captive power plant as part of the published project design. Total withdrew in 2008 over political risk; the project was later reassigned (CNPC, then PetroPars) and is presumed cancelled, but the design was published while the project was live, which is a YES on design per SOP.

T100001048168.name: Khor Al-Zubair FSRU
hw: Dual-fuel diesel-electric (DFDE) generating engines aboard the FSRU (Excelerate Acadia / Hull 3407, HD Hyundai-built, 170,000 m3, 1 Bcf/d regas capacity) generate the vessel's own electric power for storage/regasification/hotel loads; no engine model or MW rating disclosed publicly.
notes: Excelerate Acadia (Hull 3407), the FSRU assigned to this terminal, is built with dual-fuel diesel-electric (DFDE) engines generating the vessel's own onboard electric power - a documented on-site gas-capable generation plant. This is independent of the separate fact that the terminal's regasified gas output is intended to be piped onward to feed Iraqi power plants (that relationship is NOT captive - see notes).

T100000130591.name: Aqaba Jordan FSRU
hw: Wärtsilä DFDE (dual-fuel diesel-electric) onboard generating plant with advanced boil-off gas management (current owner Energos Infrastructure's vessel-specific spec), providing the vessel's own electric power; engine count/MW not publicly disclosed.
notes: The Energos Eskimo (ex-Golar Eskimo) FSRU self-generates all of its own onboard power (Golar's fleet discloses zero purchased external electricity for any vessel) and burns predominantly non-HFO fuel (97% across the FSRU sub-fleet) - i.e. documented on-site gas-fired generation for the vessel's own operations. This is independent of the separate finding that the terminal's regasified send-out gas is piped to feed Jordan's Aqaba power plant/NEPCO grid (NOT a captive relationship - see notes).

T100000130592.name: Mina Al-Ahmadi LNG Terminal
hw: Both moored FSRUs generate their own hotel/regasification-load power on board via dual-fuel diesel-electric (DFDE) gensets designed to burn LNG boil-off gas with diesel/MDO backup: the Explorer received a 'dual-fuel diesel generator power module' in its 2015-16 Excelerate upgrade; the Golar Igloo (chartered to KNPC for this terminal) is part of Golar's fleet in which 14 of 16 vessels run Wärtsilä 50DF dual-fuel engines.
notes: Both FSRUs assigned to Mina Al-Ahmadi (Explorer, now idled; Golar Igloo, now mothballed) are self-powered vessels: their onboard DFDE gensets supply the electricity for regasification pumps and hotel load rather than drawing from Kuwait's shore grid. No vessel-specific nameplate MW figure was found for either.

T100000130593.name: Oman Qalhat LNG Terminal
hw: Mixed site. (1) On-site power-generation plant: originally four GE Frame 6 gas turbine-generators (120 MW total), replaced circa 2018-2020 by nine MAN 51/60 gas engines rated 120 MW total, supplying electricity to the LNG facility. (2) Separately, dedicated mechanical-drive gas turbines run the compressor trains: a 280 MW GE Frame 7 gas turbine drives the mixed-refrigerant compression train and a 42 MW GE Frame 6 gas turbine drives the propane compression train (added under Oman LNG's Train 3 / debottlenecking expansion).
notes: Oman LNG's Qalhat site carries BOTH captive power forms: a dedicated 120 MW on-site gas-fired power plant (now MAN 51/60 gas engines, replacing the original Frame 6 turbine-generator plant) that supplies the facility's electricity, and separate GE Frame 6/Frame 7 gas turbines that mechanically drive the refrigeration compressor trains.

T100000130594.name: QatarEnergy LNG (N)
hw: GE Frame 5C/5D and Frame 9E heavy-frame gas turbines mechanically drive the refrigeration compressor strings across this entity's Ras Laffan trains (the Qatargas-heritage side of the current QatarEnergy LNG structure): the Qatargas II mega-trains use Frame 9E turbines (~132 MW ISO rating) via a Siemens VFD/Ansaldo motor-generator system that can also export surplus electrical power to the plant grid; the earlier trains use GE FR5C/FR5D turbines for both the mixed-refrigerant and propane refrigeration cycles.
notes: This QatarEnergy LNG entity's Ras Laffan trains are the textbook mechanical-drive LNG case: heavy-frame gas turbines (Frame 5C/5D on the older trains, Frame 9E — ~132 MW ISO — on the mega-trains) directly shaft-drive the refrigeration compressors, with the Frame 9E units' motor-generator system also able to export surplus power to the site's internal grid.

T100000130598.name: QatarEnergy LNG (S)
hw: GE Frame 7EA and Frame 9E heavy-frame gas turbines mechanically drive the refrigeration compressor strings on this entity's Ras Laffan trains (the RasGas-heritage side of the current QatarEnergy LNG structure): two Frame 7EA turbines were retrofitted with Dry Low NOx (DLN) combustion in 2011 while continuing to drive the mixed-refrigerant and propane compressor trains, and the RasGas mega-trains (Trains 6-7) use Frame 9E turbines (~132 MW ISO class) as the largest mechanical-drive application in the LNG industry, per Baker Hughes' own product literature.
notes: This QatarEnergy LNG entity's (RasGas-heritage) Ras Laffan trains mechanically drive their refrigeration compressors with heavy-frame gas turbines: two Frame 7EA units (DLN-retrofitted 2011) on the earlier trains, and Frame 9E units on the Train 6-7 mega-trains — described by the turbine vendor itself as 'the world's largest mechanical-drive application.'

T100000130601.name: Das Island LNG Terminal
hw: On-site electricity generation: an existing power plant of 5x GE Frame 5 gas turbine generators, plus a newer 36 MW power station (built Dec 2013-Mar 2015) built around a GE Frame 6 gas turbine burning both sweet and sour gas. Separately, mechanical drive: 2x GE Frame 5D gas turbine-driven turbocompressor trains (low-pressure + high-pressure casings) supplied by GE Oil & Gas for compression duty at the Das Island LNG/gas complex.
notes: Das Island (ADGAS/ADNOC LNG liquefaction complex) hosts on-site gas turbine power generation: a legacy plant of 5x GE Frame 5 gas turbines and a newer 36 MW gas-fired (GE Frame 6, sweet+sour gas) power station commissioned circa 2015, plus separate gas-turbine-driven (GE Frame 5D) turbocompressor trains for mechanical compression duty. This is captive generation and mechanical drive at the same site — a mixed installation.

T100000130605.name: Yemen LNG Terminal
hw: Heavy-duty gas turbines (a 1×100% shaftline arrangement per train, per industry technical literature) directly/mechanically drive the compressors on both Balhaf liquefaction trains; GE supplied two sets of electrical starter/helper systems — 2-pole induction motors rated 11 MW each at 3,600 rpm (four motors total, two per train) — used only to accelerate the shaft until combustion starts the gas turbine and to provide supplemental power when needed, not as the prime mover.
notes: Yemen LNG's two liquefaction trains at Balhaf are compressor-driven by heavy-duty gas turbines in a 1×100% shaftline configuration (industry-standard mechanical drive), with GE-supplied induction motors serving only as starter/helper — not power generation for the site. Mothballed since 2015 (Total-led JV, force majeure/civil conflict), but the captive-power finding is about as-built design, which persists regardless of current idle status.
